draft.title: Education Department Starts RIF Affecting About 1,300 Positions
draft.description_short: Education announced a March 11 RIF affecting nearly half its workforce; OIG later counted 1,227 RIF and 352 voluntary departures by March 31.
draft.description_medium: The Education Department announced a reduction in force on March 11, 2025, affecting about 1,300 positions and placing impacted staff on administrative leave. The department’s own release said its workforce would shift from 4,133 to roughly 2,183, a projection that also reflected voluntary departures. Education OIG later reported 1,227 RIF separations and at least 352 voluntary separations through March 31, 2025. The held entry’s count should not be presented as 1,300 completed firings.
draft.description_long: On March 11, 2025, the U.S. Department of Education announced that it had initiated a reduction in force affecting nearly half of its workforce and that impacted employees would be placed on administrative leave. The department’s release described its workforce as 4,133 at the start of the administration and projected roughly 2,183 after the actions. That projection included employees who had already accepted voluntary separation programs as well as the new RIF. The Department of Education Office of Inspector General later reported staffing changes in 16 of 17 offices and an overall reduction of at least 1,579 of 3,902 employees by March 31, 2025: 1,227 employees separated through RIF actions and at least 352 through voluntary options. GAO separately documented that about half of the Office for Civil Rights staff were placed on paid administrative leave and that later court orders affected the RIF. The original statement that DOGE fired 1,300 employees should be replaced with an accurately attributed announcement and counts distinguishing positions affected, completed RIF separations, and voluntary departures.
